# DocVQA Skill

## Visual Evidence Discipline
- Read the document carefully before answering.
- Prefer the smallest exact text span that answers the question.
- When several nearby strings look similar, choose the one whose surrounding labels or layout best match the question.

## Exact Answer Discipline
- Copy names, numbers, and dates exactly as the document prints them, but write punctuation in its plain form: a hyphen for an en or em dash, a straight apostrophe for a curly one, and no added quotation marks around a span that the document does not print inside quotes. Typographic variants otherwise cause single-character mismatches.
- Prefer direct extraction over paraphrase: give the value exactly as the document prints it. For "how many / how much" questions, give the printed count rather than restating the question's noun phrase. Do not prefix the answer with the label the question already names (no "label = value" form), and when the question itself specifies the unit, give the number alone if the document prints only the number. Keep any unit or symbol the document prints together with the value (a percent sign or currency symbol shown on the number).
- Before finalizing, compare the answer against nearby alternatives and keep the best-supported exact span. Confirm that the characters you are about to emit are actually printed on the page: an answer assembled out of the question's own words, or a plausible-sounding phrase you cannot point to in the image, is a guess — go back and find the document's printed wording instead.

answer-fabricated-from-question-words.description: For a tagline question the agent returns a phrase stitched out of the question's own wording instead of the tagline printed on the page, so the span has essentially zero overlap with the gold.
answer-fabricated-from-question-words.evidence: Trajectory [12] (57431): "What is the tagline with 'Wendell Rodricks' name?" → "Saris with Wendell Rodricks' name", hard=0, soft=0. The output is assembled from the prompt's nouns plus a plausible-sounding fragment; the actual printed tagline was never extracted, so soft collapses to 0 rather than showing partial overlap.
answer-fabricated-from-question-words.label: answer-fabricated-from-question-words

attempts.approach: Same revision adds an explicit clause forbidding added quotation marks around a span the document does not print inside quotes.

answer-includes-typographic-quotes.description: The agent wraps the extracted span in typographic quotation marks (and sometimes adds a conjunction) that the gold span does not contain, breaking near-exact match.
answer-includes-typographic-quotes.evidence: Trajectory [12] (51134): returned "“Redefining” Scientific Terms" (soft 0.931) — curly quotes around "Redefining" cause the mismatch; Trajectory [4] (596): returned "“Soda water” and “soda pop”" (soft 0.852) — added quotation marks and conjunction inflate the span.
answer-includes-typographic-quotes.examples_state_evidence: In the 'Copy names, numbers, and dates exactly' bullet, the clause 'no added quotation marks around a span that the document does not print inside quotes' is abstract prose with no concrete quoted-vs-unquoted example span attached.
answer-includes-typographic-quotes.label: answer-includes-typographic-quotes

date-answer-truncated-to-year.description: For a "when was ... presented" question the agent emits a bare year that scores zero against the gold, indicating either that the printed date is fuller (month/day dropped) or that another entry's year was read.
date-answer-truncated-to-year.evidence: Trajectory [1] (60454): "When was the Award presented?" → "1988", hard=0, soft=0. A year-only span against a fuller printed date falls below the ANLS clip threshold, and no surrounding date text was captured.
date-answer-truncated-to-year.label: date-answer-truncated-to-year

diagram-number-wrong-value.description: For a "diagram no." question the agent returns an identifier that does not match the printed diagram number (possible Roman-vs-Arabic or wrong figure marker).
diagram-number-wrong-value.evidence: Trajectory [4] (62840): "What is the diagram no.?" answered "I" with hard=0 and soft=0, so the returned identifier is unrelated to the gold diagram number.
diagram-number-wrong-value.label: diagram-number-wrong-value

digit-string-single-character-diff.description: Agent answers a specifically-keyed numeric field (voice-mail extension) but the returned digit string differs from the gold by one digit character, so the span never reaches exact match even though the correct label was located.
digit-string-single-character-diff.evidence: Trajectory [13] (7621): "What is the Voice mail number of Bill Duffy?" answered "68909" with hard 0.0 / soft 0.8 (1 character distance on a 5-character span), and soft only 0.6 in the gate baseline; the surrounding label/value block was targeted correctly, so the residual error is a single unresolved digit rather than a field-selection mistake.
digit-string-single-character-diff.label: digit-string-single-character-diff

attempts.approach: Revised the "copy names/numbers/dates exactly" bullet to keep the span's own boundaries and forbid adding a leading article ("the","a") or a unit/symbol ("%", "$") that the document does not print with the value.

Revised the "direct extraction over paraphrase" bullet to forbid a "label = value" prefix and forbid re-appending a unit the question itself supplies (when the document prints only the number), while keeping symbols/units the document prints with the value.

extra-unprinted-symbol-or-article-added.description: Agent appends a currency symbol that the question supplies but the document does not print, so the span overruns the gold by one character and misses near-exact match.
extra-unprinted-symbol-or-article-added.evidence: Trajectory [15] (58680): "What is the TOTAL QUOTATION amount of 'Weekly Activity Report' in $?" → "$270.00", hard=0, soft=0.857 (=1−1/7, a one-character surplus); the document prints the figure without the dollar sign.
extra-unprinted-symbol-or-article-added.examples_state_evidence: The scope clauses live inside the same "Prefer direct extraction over paraphrase" bullet ("Do not prefix the answer with the label the question already names (no 'label = value' form)", "give the number alone if the document prints only the number", "Keep any unit or symbol the document prints together with the value"). These are abstract rules stated in parentheses; no concrete 'X' not 'Y' example pair is attached.
extra-unprinted-symbol-or-article-added.label: extra-unprinted-symbol-or-article-added
extra-unprinted-symbol-or-article-added.resolve_evidence: Trajectory [10] 58687: question asks CURRENT INVOICE amount 'in $'; the agent returned '245.01' with no appended '$', matching the gold (hard 1.0) — the question-supplied symbol was correctly not added. Trajectory [8] 50837 kept the printed '43%'. Both trigger and correctly handle the symbol-vs-printed-value scenario.

max-count-table-row-misidentified.description: For a "who has the most/most often" question over a table the agent names the wrong row instead of comparing the printed counts and selecting the true maximum.
max-count-table-row-misidentified.evidence: Trajectory 1 [58750]: "Who has attended the most no. Of Investor Services Committee meetings?" answered "K. R. Nair" but scored hard 0 / soft 0, i.e. the named person is not the row holding the highest meeting count.
max-count-table-row-misidentified.label: max-count-table-row-misidentified
max-count-table-row-misidentified.resolve_evidence: Trajectory [3] (64547): "Based on this data people of which gender (men or women) are more likely to use sugar with foods other than beverages?" → "Women", hard=1, soft=1. The batch contains a compare-values-and-pick-the-maximum question over tabulated data and the agent selected the true larger category correctly.

attempts.approach: Added an Exact Answer Discipline bullet to answer with the requested span alone, dropping unrequested adjacent material (parenthetical acronyms, bracketed/currency figures, qualifiers), scoping 'what is obtained/what is called' questions to the label only.

Revised the "direct extraction over paraphrase" bullet to scope "how many / how much" questions to the printed count alone (preserving a printed unit), instead of restating the question's noun phrase.

Revised the "smallest exact text span" bullet to drop a label word printed separately from the value (e.g. return the numeral alone for a page number) while carving out contiguous printed stamps that form one indivisible value. Root-cause targeting is correct, but the "give the value itself" wording is over-broad — the gate candidate shows it caused over-stripping regressions on 18831 ("September 28" date truncated, soft 0.667) and 59796 ('11" high, 10" wide' dimensions trimmed, soft 0.889), so the scoping needs tightening to label words only.

Extended the 'direct extraction over paraphrase' bullet to cover binary yes/no (Did/Is/Was/...) questions, instructing the agent to answer with the Yes/No the document shows and stop unless the question also asks for a supporting detail.

overlong-answer-includes-adjacent-contex.description: Agent returns the correct answer but appends an unrequested trailing descriptor, so the span overruns the gold and fails near-exact match.
overlong-answer-includes-adjacent-contex.evidence: Trajectory [5] (61503): 'Which is the rent-a-car advertised?' answered 'Fairway Rent-A-Car System of Hawaii'; the appended ' System of Hawaii' pushes the 34-char span roughly 0.5 normalized distance from the gold (soft=0).
overlong-answer-includes-adjacent-contex.examples_state_evidence: The 'Prefer direct extraction over paraphrase' bullet (the accepted overlong fix) states only abstract rules ('no label = value form', 'give the printed count rather than restating the question's noun phrase'); no concrete (correct, incorrect) span pair is attached.
overlong-answer-includes-adjacent-contex.label: overlong-answer-includes-adjacent-context

plural-question-omits-additional-values.description: When the question asks for plural/multiple values printed on the page, the agent returns only one of them and omits the others.
plural-question-omits-additional-values.evidence: Trajectory [11] (63109): "What are the dates written near L.A.?" answered "4-5-52" (single date) with soft=0.667, indicating the gold contains more dates that were not included.
plural-question-omits-additional-values.label: plural-question-omits-additional-values

proper-noun-single-character-misread.description: Agent locates the correct proper-noun span but renders one character differently, missing near-exact match.
proper-noun-single-character-misread.evidence: Trajectory [5] 57321: question asks which segment has higher 'segment assets'; answer 'Cigarettes and Tobacco Products' scores hard 0 / soft 0.968 = 1−1/31, i.e. the correct row was found but a single character differs from the gold (e.g. plural/case/one-letter variant of the printed label).
proper-noun-single-character-misread.label: proper-noun-single-character-misread

attempts.approach: Extended the "copy names, numbers, and dates exactly" bullet to instruct rendering punctuation in plain form (hyphen for en/em dash, straight apostrophe for curly) without altering span boundaries or words.

typographic-punctuation-variant-in-span.description: Agent extracts the correct span but renders an internal dash or apostrophe in a typographic form that differs from the printed/gold characters, costing a single-character near-exact match.
typographic-punctuation-variant-in-span.evidence: Trajectory [8] (37229): "For when is the meeting ... scheduled?" answered "April 4–5, 1970" with soft 0.933 = exactly 1 character off over a 15-char span, i.e. the en dash. Trajectory [5] (56785): "What is written in bold capital letters?" answered "MEXICO '72" with soft 0.9 = exactly 1 character off over a 10-char span, i.e. the apostrophe glyph. Both spans are otherwise verbatim from the page.
typographic-punctuation-variant-in-span.examples_state_evidence: Same bullet gives only the character-substitution rule ('a hyphen for an en or em dash, a straight apostrophe for a curly one') — no concrete correct/incorrect span pair demonstrating a specific printed span.
typographic-punctuation-variant-in-span.label: typographic-punctuation-variant-in-span

attempts.approach: Added a Visual Evidence Discipline bullet to bind each value to the immediately adjacent label and separate look-alike neighbours such as phone vs. fax.

wrong-neighbor-field-in-label-value-bloc.description: Agent answers a specifically-keyed question with a value from a different field/row than the one the question names, giving zero overlap with the gold.
wrong-neighbor-field-in-label-value-bloc.evidence: Trajectory [7] 38920: question is specifically keyed ('heel height of women's shoes given in the desirable weights table'); answer '2-inch heels' scores hard 0 / soft 0, so the returned span came from a different row/region than the one the question points to.
wrong-neighbor-field-in-label-value-bloc.label: wrong-neighbor-field-in-label-value-block

attempts.approach: Added a Visual Evidence Discipline bullet to first locate the row/entry matching the question's exact identifier before reading across to the requested column.

wrong-row-for-numbered-identifier.description: When the question names a specific numbered record, the agent answers from a different/nearest row rather than first locking onto the entry keyed by that exact identifier.
wrong-row-for-numbered-identifier.evidence: Trajectory 2 (case 62132): "What is the location of building #53?" → "B-8", hard=0/soft=0; the coordinate appears to belong to another row in the building list, not the entry for #53.
wrong-row-for-numbered-identifier.label: wrong-row-for-numbered-identifier
wrong-row-for-numbered-identifier.resolve_evidence: Trajectory [5] (57801): "Related Party Transactions Summary numbered 6B" → correctly "Conversion of Loan to Equity"; Trajectory [8] (47071): abstract number for the name listed below "Amerson, H." → correctly 659. Both lock onto the exact identifier/position before reading across to the requested value (hard=1 in both).
